confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from web searches of aggregated cost-of-living sources: MyLifeElsewhere, Traveltables, Expat Exchange, Citycost and Expatistan. The sources disagreed. Cappuccino was about $2.3-3.5, a pint of domestic beer about $2.6 (roughly 55-58 CZK), an inexpensive meal about $9.6-10 (about 200 CZK) and a mid-range three-course meal for two about $32-44 (700-933 CZK). One outlier at $14 was discarded. Values were adjusted slightly upward for summer 2026 restaurant inflation and a CZK/USD rate of about 21-22. The Expatistan cocktail figure (about 159 CZK at a downtown club) is based on only 7 data points. The search found no glass-of-wine price for Brno, so the wine anchor is a model estimate from typical Czech/Moravian wine-bar pricing (0.15-0.2 l at about 80-100 CZK), set at roughly 1.5x the beer price. Brno is in a wine region, so prices are moderate. All accommodation anchors are general-knowledge model estimates, not checked against live listings. July is shoulder/summer season, and prices rise during events such as the Brno MotoGP and trade fairs, so accommodation is the least certain part of this estimate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Brno is the Czech Republic's second city and a university and trade-fair centre. It is noticeably cheaper than Prague and has a price level similar to Bratislava, Ostrava/Olomouc and Wrocław/Kraków in Poland. Accommodation was benchmarked against these Central European mid-sized cities, which get some summer tourism but not Prague-level demand.
